title: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for BCR::ABL1-Negative Myeloproliferative Neoplasms (MPN). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (CBC with teardrop poikilocytosis and leukoerythroblastic picture, bone marrow aspirate/core with reticulin/trichrome fibrosis grading, driver mutation molecular testing for JAK2 V617F / exon 12, CALR exon 9, MPL W515, myeloid NGS panel for ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1, serum EPO level, abdominal ultrasound for splenomegaly) -> Entity Stratification: Primary Myelofibrosis (PMF) / Post-PV / Post-ET MF vs Polycythemia Vera (PV) vs Essential Thrombocythemia (ET) -> Myelofibrosis Risk Stratification (DIPSS / MIPSS70: Low, Intermediate-1, Intermediate-2, High): Intermediate-2 / High Risk -> Allogeneic HCT evaluation (only curative approach) + JAK Inhibitor therapy: Ruxolitinib 5-25 mg BID for symptomatic splenomegaly; Fedratinib 400 mg daily; Pacritinib 200 mg BID (preferred for severe thrombocytopenia platelets <50,000/mcL); Momelotinib 200 mg daily (preferred for intermediate/high risk MF with symptomatic anemia Hb <10 g/dL) -> Polycythemia Vera Risk Stratification: Low Risk (age <60 and no thrombosis history) -> Phlebotomy to maintain Hct <45% + Low-dose aspirin 81-100 mg daily; High Risk (age >=60 or prior arterial/venous thrombosis) -> Phlebotomy + Aspirin + Cytoreductive therapy: Hydroxyurea 500-1000 mg daily (Category 1) or Ropeginterferon alfa-2b (BESREMi Category 1); Ruxolitinib for hydroxyurea resistance or intolerance -> Essential Thrombocythemia: Risk-adapted therapy (Very Low, Low, Intermediate, High); Hydroxyurea or Anagrelide. References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Myeloproliferative Neoplasms Version 2.2026 (July 2026).

a.text: DIPSS (Dynamic IPSS) uses age >65 years, WBC >25 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin <10 g/dL, circulating blasts >=1%, and constitutional symptoms; MIPSS70 adds high molecular risk mutations (ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1) and fibrosis grade. Low / Intermediate-1 disease is observed; Intermediate-2 / High disease is referred for allogeneic HCT evaluation.

b.text: COMFORT-I/II trials: ruxolitinib achieved >=35% spleen volume reduction and constitutional symptom control in intermediate-2/high-risk MF; starting dose is set by baseline platelet count (5-25 mg BID). Fedratinib 400 mg daily is a Category 1 alternative including after ruxolitinib failure (JAKARTA/JAKARTA2).

c.text: PERSIST-1/2 trials: pacritinib 200 mg BID retained full-dose JAK2/IRAK1 inhibition in MF with severe thrombocytopenia (platelets <50 x 10^9/L) without myelosuppressive dose reductions. MOMENTUM trial: momelotinib 200 mg daily (dual ACVR1/JAK inhibition) improved anemia and transfusion independence while shrinking spleen in symptomatic anemic MF.

d.text: CYTO-PV trial: maintaining hematocrit strictly below 45% with therapeutic phlebotomy reduces cardiovascular death and major thrombosis in PV. RESPONSE trial: ruxolitinib produced hematocrit control plus >=35% spleen reduction in hydroxyurea-resistant or intolerant PV.

e.text: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is the only curative modality for myelofibrosis; HLA typing and unrelated-donor search should begin at Intermediate-2/High-risk assignment or at first sign of leukemic progression. JAK inhibitor therapy before HCT controls splenomegaly and symptoms but does not replace transplant evaluation.

nodes.name: Workup
nodes.title: MPN: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm a BCR::ABL1-negative MPN and gather the morphology, molecular, and laboratory data that drive entity assignment and risk stratification.
bullets: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential and manual peripheral blood smear review: leukoerythroblastic picture, teardrop poikilocytes (dacryocytes), giant hypogranular platelets.
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine core biopsy: morphologic evaluation, cellularity, megakaryocyte clustering and atypia, reticulin and collagen silver staining with fibrosis grade MF-0 to MF-3.

Molecular driver testing: sequential or multiplex assay for JAK2 V617F (present in about 95% of PV and 55-60% of ET and PMF); if negative, test JAK2 exon 12 for suspected PV, or CALR exon 9 insertion/deletion and MPL codon 515 for ET and PMF. Triple-negative MPN requires deep evaluation to rule out reactive causes or other myeloid neoplasms.
Myeloid NGS prognostic panel: ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1 (high molecular risk mutations associated with accelerated leukemic transformation and inferior overall survival).

Laboratory baseline and organ imaging: serum erythropoietin (subnormal EPO is a major WHO criterion for PV), serum ferritin, iron panel, LDH, uric acid; abdominal ultrasound or CT to measure spleen volume and span in centimeters.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed - Proceed to MPN Subtype Classification

nodes.name: MPN subtype
nodes.title: MPN entity stratification (PMF / PV / ET)
nodes.description: Assign the WHO MPN entity from marrow morphology, fibrosis grade, driver mutation, hemoglobin/hematocrit, platelet count, and EPO level. Entity determines which risk model and therapy pathway applies.
bullets: Myelofibrosis (primary MF, post-PV MF, post-ET MF): marrow fibrosis MF-1 or higher with megakaryocyte atypia, leukoerythroblastosis with dacryocytes, splenomegaly, and often anemia or leukocytosis.
Polycythemia vera: elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit with subnormal serum EPO, JAK2 V617F or exon 12 mutation, hypercellular marrow with panmyelosis.

Essential thrombocythemia: sustained thrombocytosis with megakaryocyte proliferation, JAK2 V617F, CALR exon 9, or MPL W515 driver (or triple-negative after exclusion of reactive causes), without significant fibrosis or PV features.

nodes.name: MF risk
nodes.title: Myelofibrosis risk stratification (DIPSS / MIPSS70)
nodes.description: Assign DIPSS / MIPSS70 risk from age, counts, blasts, symptoms, karyotype, fibrosis grade, and high molecular risk mutations. Risk separates observation from HCT evaluation plus JAK inhibitor therapy.
bullets: Low / Intermediate-1 risk, asymptomatic: observation with symptom-directed care and serial spleen, blood count, and symptom-burden monitoring.

Intermediate-2 / High risk (symptomatic disease, cytopenias, constitutional symptoms, circulating blasts, adverse karyotype, or high molecular risk mutations): allogeneic HCT evaluation plus JAK inhibitor therapy tailored to platelets and anemia.

options.label: Intermediate-2 / High Risk (symptomatic, cytopenias, constitutional symptoms)

nodes.name: MF symptom profile
nodes.title: Intermediate-2 / High-risk MF: cytopenia and symptom profile
nodes.description: Select the JAK inhibitor by the dominant clinical problem: severe thrombocytopenia, symptomatic anemia, or splenomegaly with constitutional symptoms and adequate platelets. All three arms include HCT evaluation.
bullets: Platelets below 50 x 10^9/L: pacritinib keeps full dose where other JAK inhibitors require myelosuppressive reductions.
Symptomatic anemia with hemoglobin below 10 g/dL with or without splenomegaly: momelotinib addresses anemia, transfusion burden, and spleen together.
Splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms with platelets at or above 50 x 10^9/L: ruxolitinib or fedratinib.

options.label: Symptomatic Anemia (Hb < 10 g/dL) with or without splenomegaly
Splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms, platelets >= 50 x 10^9/L

nodes.name: PV risk
nodes.title: Polycythemia vera risk stratification
nodes.description: Assign PV thrombotic risk from age and thrombosis history. Low risk is managed with phlebotomy plus aspirin; high risk adds cytoreductive therapy.
bullets: Low risk: age below 60 years with NO history of arterial or venous thrombosis.
High risk: age 60 years or older, or any prior arterial or venous thrombosis.

options.label: Low Risk (Age < 60 and NO history of thrombosis)
High Risk (Age >= 60 or prior arterial/venous thrombosis)

nodes.name: ET risk
nodes.title: Essential thrombocythemia risk stratification
nodes.description: Assign ET thrombotic risk from age, thrombosis history, and JAK2 status. Very low / low risk is managed with observation or aspirin; intermediate / high risk adds cytoreduction.
bullets: Very low / low risk: age below 60, no prior thrombosis, JAK2-unmutated or mutated without additional risk factors.
Intermediate / high risk: age 60 or older, or any prior arterial or venous thrombosis.

options.label: Very Low / Low Risk (Age < 60, no thrombosis)
Intermediate / High Risk (Age >= 60 or prior thrombosis)

nodes.name: MF low-risk management
nodes.title: Low / Intermediate-1 MF: observation and symptom-directed therapy
nodes.description: Observation pathway for asymptomatic low / Intermediate-1 myelofibrosis with escalation triggers for progressive symptoms or splenomegaly.
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / MF / Low Risk / Observation
bullets: Observation (watch-and-wait) with serial CBC, spleen measurement, and validated symptom-burden assessment; repeat DIPSS / MIPSS70 on clinical change.
Symptom-directed therapy with low-dose aspirin for vasomotor or thrombotic symptoms when not contraindicated by bleeding risk or severe thrombocytopenia.
Consider pegylated interferon alfa or ruxolitinib for progressive symptoms or enlarging splenomegaly; re-stratify to the Intermediate-2 / High-risk pathway on progression.
Counsel on infection, bleeding, thrombosis, and leukemic-transformation warning signs at each visit.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: MF pacritinib
nodes.title: Intermediate-2 / High-risk MF with severe thrombocytopenia: pacritinib
nodes.description: Category 1 preferred JAK inhibitor for MF with platelets below 50 x 10^9/L, with concurrent allogeneic HCT evaluation.
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / MF / High Risk / Pacritinib
bullets: Pacritinib 200 mg PO BID, Category 1 Preferred for severe thrombocytopenia based on PERSIST-1/2 trials.
Full-dose JAK2/IRAK1 inhibition without myelosuppressive dose reductions; monitor CBC, coagulation, bleeding, QTc, and gastrointestinal tolerance.
Evaluate for allogeneic HCT in parallel: HLA typing and donor search at Intermediate-2/High-risk assignment (only curative approach).
Track spleen response and symptom burden; manage drug interactions before dose changes.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: MF momelotinib
nodes.title: Intermediate-2 / High-risk MF with symptomatic anemia: momelotinib
nodes.description: Category 1 preferred JAK inhibitor for MF with symptomatic anemia (Hb below 10 g/dL), with concurrent allogeneic HCT evaluation.
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / MF / High Risk / Momelotinib
bullets: Momelotinib 200 mg PO daily, Category 1 Preferred for symptomatic anemia based on the MOMENTUM trial.
Dual ACVR1/JAK inhibition improves anemia, reduces transfusion burden, and shrinks spleen; monitor hemoglobin, transfusion need, CBC, LFTs, and gastrointestinal tolerance.
Evaluate for allogeneic HCT in parallel: HLA typing and donor search at Intermediate-2/High-risk assignment (only curative approach).
Reassess iron status and bleeding sources before attributing persistent anemia to MF alone.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: MF ruxolitinib
nodes.title: Intermediate-2 / High-risk MF with splenomegaly: ruxolitinib or fedratinib
nodes.description: Category 1 preferred JAK inhibitor therapy for splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms with platelets at or above 50 x 10^9/L, with concurrent allogeneic HCT evaluation.
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / MF / High Risk / Ruxolitinib
bullets: Ruxolitinib 5-25 mg PO BID based on baseline platelet count, Category 1 Preferred per COMFORT-I/II trials; monitor CBC, spleen volume, symptom score, lipids, and infection risk.
Alternative: fedratinib 400 mg PO daily, Category 1 (including after ruxolitinib failure); monitor thiamine, gastrointestinal tolerance, CBC, LFTs, and renal function.
Evaluate for allogeneic HCT in parallel: HLA typing and donor search at Intermediate-2/High-risk assignment (only curative approach).
Taper rather than abruptly stop JAK inhibitor therapy to avoid symptom-rebound cytokine flare.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: PV low-risk therapy
nodes.title: Low-risk PV: phlebotomy plus low-dose aspirin
nodes.description: Phlebotomy plus aspirin pathway for low-risk polycythemia vera (age below 60, no thrombosis history).
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / PV / Low Risk / Phlebotomy
bullets: Therapeutic phlebotomy to maintain hematocrit strictly below 45% (Hct <45%); monitor hematocrit, CBC, ferritin, and iron symptoms between sessions.
Low-dose aspirin 81-100 mg PO daily unless contraindicated by bleeding risk or aspirin intolerance.
Aggressive cardiovascular risk factor modification: blood pressure, lipids, diabetes control, smoking cessation, weight and activity counseling.
Escalate to the high-risk pathway with cytoreductive therapy on thrombosis, age transition to 60 or older, progressive leukocytosis or thrombocytosis, or enlarging splenomegaly.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: PV high-risk therapy
nodes.title: High-risk PV: phlebotomy plus aspirin plus cytoreduction
nodes.description: Cytoreductive pathway for high-risk polycythemia vera (age 60 or older, or prior arterial/venous thrombosis) with second-line ruxolitinib for hydroxyurea resistance or intolerance.
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / PV / High Risk / Cytoreduction
bullets: Phlebotomy to target hematocrit below 45% (Hct <45%) plus low-dose aspirin 81-100 mg PO daily as the backbone of high-risk care.
Cytoreductive therapy: hydroxyurea 500-1000 mg PO daily, Category 1 Preferred; monitor CBC, MCV, LFTs, renal function, skin and mucocutaneous tolerance, and fertility plans.
Alternative first-line cytoreduction: ropeginterferon alfa-2b (BESREMi), Category 1 Preferred, particularly for younger patients; monitor CBC, LFTs, thyroid function, mood, and autoimmune history.
Second-line: ruxolitinib for hydroxyurea resistance or intolerance per the RESPONSE trial (hematocrit control plus spleen reduction); monitor CBC and infection risk.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: ET low-risk therapy
nodes.title: Very low / Low-risk ET: observation or low-dose aspirin
nodes.description: Conservative pathway for very low / low-risk essential thrombocythemia (age below 60, no thrombosis history).
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / ET / Low Risk / Observation
bullets: Observation or low-dose aspirin 81 mg PO daily, selected by JAK2 status, cardiovascular risk, and bleeding history.
Monitor platelet count, CBC, vasomotor symptoms (erythromelalgia, headache, paresthesia), and acquired von Willebrand risk at extreme thrombocytosis.
Aggressive cardiovascular risk factor modification at each visit.
Escalate to cytoreduction on thrombosis, age transition to 60 or older, or progressive symptoms.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.name: ET high-risk therapy
nodes.title: Intermediate / High-risk ET: aspirin plus cytoreduction
nodes.description: Cytoreductive pathway for intermediate / high-risk essential thrombocythemia (age 60 or older, or prior thrombosis).
nodes.path: Myeloproliferative Neoplasms / ET / High Risk / Cytoreduction
bullets: Low-dose aspirin 81-100 mg PO daily plus cytoreduction unless contraindicated by bleeding risk.
Hydroxyurea 500-1000 mg PO daily, Category 1 Preferred; monitor CBC, LFTs, renal function, and mucocutaneous tolerance.

Alternatives for younger or pregnant patients: anagrelide 0.5 mg PO QID with cardiac and platelet monitoring, or interferon alfa / peginterferon alfa (Pegasys) with CBC, LFT, thyroid, and mood monitoring.
Monitor platelet control, thrombotic and bleeding events, and fibrosis or leukemic-transformation signs on long-term therapy.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
